To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the facies pattern of the studied sections was formed under the influence of a high energetic environment, and was strongly obscured by an intense process of onshore transport and redeposition of material.

the facies pattern of the Malynysty Formation is characterized by the presence of an oncolitic-fenestral complex and a parabiostrome of massive stromatoporoïds, which underlie and overlie it respectively, and that the latter is interpreted as a product of the redeposition of material of outer shelf areas.

the facies succession of the Late Silurian Malynivtsy biostromes is controlled by the distance from the shoreline, with the facies belts of shoals and back-shoal flats alternating, and that these facies are strongly affected by the process of onshore transport of sediment and organisms, which is controlled by the intensity of wave action.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sedimentary history of the Upper Silurian stromatoporoid bioherms of the Podolia region (Ukraine), based on the morphometrical analysis.

sedimentary processes that affected the distribution of stromatoporid biostromes and their morphometrical features, and it also contributes to our understanding of the role of stromatoporids in carbonate platform sedimentology.

the sedimentary history of two biostromal complexes of different genesis, and the morphometrical approach to the analysis of stromatoporid accumulations has proven to be useful in reconstructing the depositional conditions of the host facies and the processes of biostromal accumulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sedimentary history of the studied biostromes is governed by the interplay between the depositional processes in the area of shoals, where the main accumulation of biogenic material took place, and the processes of onshore redepositing, which caused the formation of the parabiostromal complexes.
the studied stromatoporoid parabiostromal complexes were formed by redeposited material from the outer shelf, whereas the autoparabiostrome of the shoal zone was formed by autochthonous material.
the sedimentary history of biostromes reflects the history of depositional environment, which was strongly affected by high energetic events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

stromatoporoid parabiostromal facies are not a product of autochthonous growth of the organisms in the back-shoal zone, but are rather a result of exhumation and transport of autochthonously grown specimens from outer-shelf areas.

the sedimentary patterns of the Malynysty Formation reflect a complex interplay of various processes, such as wave action, storm activity and sediment reworking, which were responsible for the distribution of the biostromes and the sedimentary facies of the section.

the sedimentary history of biostromes in Podolia is controlled by a combination of factors such as (1) the depositional setting, (2) the morphological features of the biota, and (3) the intensity of high energy episodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stromatoporoids are very sensitive to environmental changes.
morphometrical analysis can be used to reconstruct depositional settings of stromatoporid biostromes and to distinguish between parabiostromal and autoparabiostrome facies.

the morphometrical analysis can be a powerful tool in reconstructing sedimentary history of carbonate deposits, especially when the facies succession is strongly disturbed by the process of onshore transport of carbonate debris.
